text.p: The Swiss share market ended two days of decline, closing higher after fluctuating during much of the session, but dealers said there was no clear direction to trading and nervousness remained high.

The situation was likely to remain unsettled ahead of various U.S. economic data and the U.S. Federal Reserve Board's meeting, one trader noted. Another said Swiss shares were likely to continue tracking developments on Wall Street.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed 15.2 points, or 0.34 percent, higher at 4,535.1 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index was up 8.04 points, or 0.28 percent, to 2,879.50.

CS Group, Alusuisse and ABB were among the winners of the day. Alusuisse rose 32 francs to 1,242. CS Group, which jumped 3.50 francs to 166.25, was sought after a period of weakness, one dealer noted. ABB was up 29 francs to 1,719.
Actively-traded Novartis registered shares rose 11 francs to 1,749.
Nestle, SMH and Ciba were among the most prominent losers. Nestle was under temporary heavy pressure after a flurry of sell orders, a dealer said. The stock ended down 15 francs at 1,585.
Ciba slumped 2.75 francs to 115.75. One dealer said most investors now believed the stock was overvalued, even when it was initially issued at 110.00 francs.
SMH bearers slid 27 francs to 823. Adecco was up two francs to 452.00. Dealers said 1996 figures released today were in line with expectations.
UBS bearer shares added three francs to end at 1,293.
